answer: Hardware-enclave attestation curbs Sybil attacks by anchoring each agent's identity to a physical secure cryptoprocessor. Autonomous agents managing an agricultural vine, coastal reef, or tracking a falcon must supply remote attestation proofs rooted in private silicon keys. An attacker incurs the concrete capital cost of buying discrete microchips for every alias. However, this dependency centralizes trust in chip vendors and fails if hardware extraction exploits compromise root signing keys.
